item.title: After Carmen: Ohio State’s Offensive Flaws Exposed by Indiana in Big Ten Championship Game Loss
item.description: Matchup games expose a team's flaws. In a matchup game against No. 2 (soon to be No. 1) Indiana, Ohio State's shortcomings on offense were exposed. The Buckeyes settled for a field goal once in the red zone, missed a field goal another time and were stopped on fourth down on a third. item.title: Indiana Wide Receiver Charlie Becker Appears to Mock Ohio State With Postgame “O-H” Podium Gesture After Big Ten Championship
item.description: Indiana wideout Charlie Becker picked his moment — twice — on Saturday night in Indianapolis. The sophomore led the No. 2 Hoosiers with six catches for 126 yards in their 13–10 win over No. 1 Ohio State, including the back-breaking 33-yard grab on 3rd-and-6 with 2:41 left that helped seal the Buckeyes’ first loss of the season. item.title: Social Reactions: Ohio State Loses to Indiana in the Big Ten Championship Game for the Buckeyes' First Loss of the Season
item.description: In the new era of college football and with the expanded CFP, it's hard to be perfect. That said, every loss hurts, especially for a program like Ohio State. The Buckeyes suffered their first loss of the season Saturday night in Indianapolis, falling to Indiana, 13-10. It was the first time that OSU trailed in the second half this season, and the first time they had to deal with major adversity in the fourth quarter. item.title: Five Things: Indiana Bests Ohio State in B1G Title Game As Offensive Line, Red Zone Offense, And Special Teams Falter Versus Hoosiers
item.description: Looking to capture its first B1G title in five years, No. 1 Ohio State struggled on offense and special teams, and gave up a couple back-breaking third down conversions on defense as No. 2 Indiana held off the Buckeyes, 13-10, last night in Lucas Oil Stadium. The loss snapped Ohio State's 16-game winning streak dating back to last season's run through the College Football Playoff and cost the Buckeyes a No. 1 seed in this year's CFP seeding. item.title: Ohio State Earns No. 2 Seed in College Football Playoff, Will Face Texas A&M or Miami in the Cotton Bowl
item.description: Ohio State is the No. 2 seed in the College Football Playoff. The CFP committee selected Ohio State as the No. 2 seed behind undefeated Indiana, which just beat the Buckeyes 13-10 in the Big Ten Championship Game. Ohio State will face the winner of Texas A&M vs. Miami in the Cotton Bowl. item.title: Presser Bullets: Brian Hartline to Remain Play Caller for College Football Playoff, Ohio State Will "Respond Like Men" to Loss
item.description: Avoiding finger-pointing after a loss is critical for the health of a locker room. Ohio State fell for the first time this season in the Big Ten Championship Game, losing 13-10 to Indiana. In his Sunday press conference, after finding out that the No. 2 Buckeyes would play their College Football Playoff quarterfinal game at the Cotton Bowl, Day said that his team will "respond like men" and avoid finger-pointing and self-pity. item.title: Press Coverage: Ohio State Still Favored to Win National Championship Despite Challenging College Football Playoff Path As No. 2 Seed
item.description: Ohio State digested its Indiana loss in a span of 16 hours. The Buckeyes will dive into the film, review their flaws and work to address them. Otherwise, it's College Football Playoff time. Ryan Day's squad learned its seeding and quarterfinal location on Sunday, as the Buckeyes earned the No. 2 spot in the CFP and will play in the Cotton Bowl against either No. 7 Texas A&M or No. 10 Miami. item.title: Ohio State Placed in Cotton Bowl Over Orange Bowl to Avoid Possible Home Game for Miami
item.description: Ohio State will play in the Cotton Bowl rather than the Orange Bowl to avoid the possibility of the Buckeyes having to play Miami in the Hurricanes’ home stadium. item.description: Ohio State is back on its quest to repeat as national champions. item.title: Ohio State Safety Caleb Downs Wins 2025 Lott IMPACT Trophy
item.description: Caleb Downs is a great player, on and off the field. Widely regarded as one of the best defensive players in college football and a captain for the Buckeyes this season, Downs is a leader for Ohio State, on and off the field. Sunday night was yet another example of that, as Downs was awarded the Lott IMPACT Trophy.
